archetypes.name: output-consumer-graph
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims the new HTML marker is 'purely additive' but names only four consumers of final-summary.md; at least two additional files (test-render-cost-line-callsites.sh, test-refresh-run-logs.sh) also reference the file and are not audited in the plan.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan identifies four consumers of final-summary.md (ship-pr.sh, refresh-run-logs.sh, verify-run-log-completeness.sh, audit-scan-run.sh) and asserts the new HTML comment marker is purely additive, but the repository contains additional files that reference final-summary.md (scripts/test-render-cost-line-callsites.sh, scripts/test-refresh-run-logs.sh) which are not analyzed in the plan. Grep the full repo for final-summary.md references and for any script that reads the larch: marker namespace broadly (e.g., a pattern matching 'larch:' anywhere in the file body) to confirm no unlisted consumer is affected by the new larch:final-summary-fallback v1 marker. Pay special attention to scripts that consume the entire file body rather than anchoring on the first non-empty heading line, since those would encounter both the banner text and the new HTML marker. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-failure-mechanics
archetypes.rationale: The plan delegates both new test setups to 'whichever already-used failure-forcing pattern is in the harness today,' but the design-side harness has no existing forced-render-failure case and sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT to the real repo root, making the delegation ambiguous and risking an incompatible mechanism choice.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's test additions for both harnesses rely on an 'already-used pattern' for forcing invoke_render failure, but skills/design/scripts/test-render-final-summary.sh contains no existing failure-forcing test case and points CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT at the real repo root where render-run-summary.sh genuinely exists — so the redirect approach (pointing to a missing script path) must be an entirely new setup, not a reuse. The implement-side harness (skills/implement/scripts/test-write-final-report.sh lines 44-55) copies render-run-summary.sh into a temp plugin dir at setup time, so a stub placed before that copy would be overwritten; failure must be forced by replacing the copy after setup or by writing the stub after the copy step, and the plan does not specify this ordering. Verify also that forcing both Stage-1 and Stage-2 to fail in the implement-side test reliably reaches compose_self_fallback given the set +e / set -e guards and the rr/rr2 conditional at lines 491-507, and that the harness's STATUS=ok / assert_contains idioms (lines 15-16, 42) are the idiomatic assertions the plan should prescribe. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: marker-placement-precision
archetypes.rationale: The implement-side compose_self_fallback writes to body_tmp inside a brace block and then appends notes_tmp externally at lines 479-482; the plan's 'after line 477' insertion must be verified to land inside the closing brace and not between the function and the notes append, and the design-side cancelled-outline ordering must be explicitly confirmed.
archetypes.prompt_body: The design-side compose_self_fallback (render-final-summary.sh lines 358-390) uses a single brace block redirected to out_file, making both insertions unambiguous; but the implement-side (write-final-report.sh lines 443-478) ends its brace block at line 478 and appends notes_tmp to body_tmp outside the function at lines 479-482, so the plan's 'after line 477' insertion must be confirmed to land on a line between 477 and 478 (inside the closing brace), not after line 478 where it would appear between function output and appended notes. For the design side, verify that inserting the new HTML marker between the run-summary v=1 line (385) and the cancelled-outline conditional (386-388) preserves the existing harness assertion in test-render-final-summary.sh lines 54-57 that the cancel-site bullet appears after the sentinel, and that the new marker does not displace or interleave with that bullet. Also confirm that placing the banner as the second non-empty line (after the heading printf on line 361/445) leaves the first non-empty line as the outcome heading, which is the invariant required by the first-line parsers in verify-run-log-completeness.sh and audit-scan-run.sh. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
